label: lem:antiderivatives_diff_constant
title: Two antiderivatives differ by a constant
statement: Let $f : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ and let $F, G$ both be antiderivatives of $f$ on $\mathrm{Ioo}\; a\; b$ (i.e.\ $\texttt{IsAntiderivativeOn}\; F\; f\; a\; b$ and $\texttt{IsAntiderivativeOn}\; G\; f\; a\; b$), with both $F$ and $G$ continuous on $\mathrm{Icc}\; a\; b$. Then $F - G$ is constant on $\mathrm{Icc}\; a\; b$, i.e., for all $x \in \mathrm{Icc}\; a\; b$, $(F - G)(x) = (F - G)(a)$.
proof: By Lemma~\ref{lem:antideriv_diff_zero_deriv}, the function $F - G$ has derivative $0$ at every $x \in \mathrm{Ioo}\; a\; b$. Moreover, $F - G$ is continuous on $\mathrm{Icc}\; a\; b$ since both $F$ and $G$ are. By Lemma~\ref{lem:zero_deriv_constant}, $(F-G)(x) = (F-G)(a)$ for all $x \in \mathrm{Icc}\; a\; b$.
